Entering experimental data for the Bayesian calibration

CVSF Process Simulator · Model V01 · guide to the Excel template, the experiment database, and the recalibration

This guide describes how experimental data of completed CVSF runs are transferred to the CVSF Process Simulator so that the model parameters can be improved continuously by Bayesian calibration. Follow the five steps; every step shows the corresponding screenshot.

1 Template
download the Excel template
2 Fill in
material system and one row per experiment
3 Upload & check
template + PSD files, check every row, add as dataset
4 Database
activate / deactivate datasets and experiments
5 Recalibrate
check the results, adopt the new model state

Which data improve which model parameters?

Measured quantity (column)Typical experimentUpdated parameters
θm (theta_m_meas)residence time distribution (RTD) of the solids μs, a, b – residence time correlation (Fit 1)
ε, α_FC (eps_meas_pct, alpha_FC_meas)filter cake test, e.g. pressure filtration cell (VDI 2762), with the PSD of the same particlesA – sphericity correction (Fit F1)
φ_RM (phi_RM_meas_pct)CVSF run: residual moisture of the product at the outlet of the filtration module, with PSD and complete operating pointB – equilibrium saturation factor (Fit F2)
One row may contain several measured quantities of the same run (e.g. θm and φ_RM). Rows are used wherever they are complete; incomplete rows are stored but ignored by the calibration until they are completed.

Step 1Download the Excel template

Start the CVSF Process Simulator (desktop icon or start_gui.bat), switch to the mode Calibration in the sidebar (Figure 1), open tab 1 · Add data, and click Excel template (Figure 2). This guide can be downloaded next to it; Show example rows displays three complete example rows in the interface.

The sidebar summarizes the calibration workflow: add data → activate/deactivate in the experiment database → recalibrate → adopt the new model state.

The template contains four sheets:

  • Instructions – short version of this guide, required columns, definitions.
  • Experiments – the sheet to be filled in (row 1: column names, row 2: units, data from row 3).
  • Example – three complete example rows (one per measured quantity), colored by column group.
  • Material system – name of the material system, solid density, surface tension of the liquid.

Step 2Fill in the template

2a · Sheet “Material system”

Use exactly the same name for all datasets of one material system (e.g. L-alanine / water). Datasets with the same name are calibrated together; a different spelling creates a new material system with a weakly informative prior.

2b · Sheet “Experiments” – one row per experiment

The sheet Example shows how complete rows look. The colors mark the column groups: grey = identification, orange = particle system (PSD), green = apparatus and operating point, yellow = measured quantities. Hovering over a column name in Excel shows its unit and description.

Fill in the sheet Experiments in the same way, starting in row 3. Only the columns required for the measured quantity of the row are needed; leave all other cells empty (do not enter 0):

ColumnUnitθm (RTD)ε / α_FC (filter cake)φ_RM (CVSF run) Remark

2c · Definitions

QuantityDefinition
theta_m_measθm = τm / τhy: mean solids residence time τm from the RTD divided by the residence time of ideal screw conveying τhy = L / (P · n_screw) over the same conveying length L (P: pitch)
eps_meas_pctfilter cake porosity = void volume / cake volume, in %
alpha_FC_measmass-related specific filter cake resistance in m/kg
phi_RM_meas_pctresidual moisture of the product at the outlet of the filtration module, wet basis: m_liquid / (m_liquid + m_solid), in %
w_solid_pctsolid mass fraction of the suspension in wt.-%
setupcurrent: frit 6 cm, transport zone 8 cm, module 14 cm; previous: frit 4.5 cm, module 13 cm
screw(a) one flight, P = 12 mm, d_i = 16 mm; (b) one flight, P = 23 mm, d_i = 21 mm; (c) two flights, P = 24 mm, d_i = 21 mm
PSD filesPSDResults_*.xlsx (PSD and agglomeration degree) and, for cuboid and needle-shaped particles, ImageDescriptors_*.xlsx (minimum/maximum Feret diameters), exported by the dynamic image analysis. Enter the file name and upload the file together with the template, or enter the full path.
Common mistakes
  • Fractions instead of percent (0.21 instead of 21 for φ_RM; 0.06 instead of 6 for w_solid).
  • Pressure difference in Pa or bar instead of mbar.
  • Residual moisture on dry basis instead of wet basis.
  • θm entered as τm in minutes instead of the dimensionless ratio.
  • Rows with ID starting with EXAMPLE are ignored – rename copied example rows.
  • PSD file name in the template differs from the uploaded file name.
The interface checks the plausibility of all values and points out values that look like wrong units.

Step 3Upload, check, and add as dataset

In tab 1 · Add data, upload the filled template (left) and all PSD files referenced in it (right; several files at once). The experiments appear in an editable table; values can still be corrected there. Below the table, the status of every row is shown:

  • usable for – which calibration stage the row informs (θm, ε/α_FC, φ_RM).
  • missing information – what is missing (e.g. PSD file not uploaded, operating point incomplete).
  • plausibility check – values outside the usual range (often a unit error).

Then enter the dataset information (material system, dataset name, operator, date of the experiments, description of special features) and click Add dataset to the experiment database. The PSD files are copied into the database folder, so the dataset remains complete even if the original files are moved.

Step 4Experiment database: activate and deactivate

Tab 2 · Experiment database lists all datasets added since model version V01. Each dataset and each single experiment has an active checkbox. Only active experiments of active datasets enter the calibration.

  • To exclude data (e.g. a run turns out to be not representative), uncheck active, enter the reason for deactivation, and click Save … changes. Deactivated data stay in the database and can be reactivated at any time.
  • Every change is written to the change log (time, user, action, reason).
  • Deleting a dataset is possible in its details, but deactivation is usually sufficient and keeps the history.
  • The storage folder can be changed (e.g. to a shared network folder of the working group) – all users then work with the same experiment database and model states.
The 33 data of the filtration study (13 RTD values, 8 filter cakes, 12 residual moistures) are already contained in the reference parameter set and are therefore not stored in the database again.

Step 5Recalibrate the model and adopt the model state

Tab 3 · Recalibrate model shows for the selected material system the current model state, whether it is outdated (active data changed since), and the number of active experiments. Click Recalibrate model with all active experiments.

Each recalibration starts again from the reference parameter set of the filtration study (prior) and uses all active experiments. Deactivated data therefore have no influence on the new model state.

Before adopting, check:
  • Do the model-vs-experiment plots improve, and are there outliers (possibly a deactivation candidate)?
  • Leave-one-out Q²: values near 1 mean good prediction of experiments not used for the calibration.
  • Notes “data hardly inform this parameter”: the parameter remains close to the prior – collect more or more varied data (e.g. different rotational screw speeds and screws for θm, different PSDs for A, different operating points for B).

Click Adopt as current model state. The model state is stored with its provenance (datasets, experiments, data fingerprint) and is marked with ★ in the parameter-set selection of the mode Simulation. Earlier model states remain available in tab 4 · Model states & parameter sets and can be reactivated at any time.

Troubleshooting

MessageCause and remedy
PSD file '…' not foundUpload the file together with the template, or enter the full path; the file name must match exactly (incl. extension).
ImageDescriptors file missingCuboid and needle-shaped particles require the ImageDescriptors file in addition to the PSDResults file.
φ_RM: … missingThe residual moisture requires the complete operating point (setup, screw, Q, w_solid, n, Δp, ϑ).
cake formation not completed (z_S1 > L_f)For this operating point the model predicts incomplete cake formation on the filter medium; the residual moisture cannot be used for B. Check Δp, Q, and n.
plausibility check …Value outside the usual range – check the unit (%, mbar, rpm).
Status “outdated”Datasets were added or (de)activated since the current model state – recalibrate.
